label: early copy phase, strongest on input s (first copied token)
explanation: Sparse (~1% of steps) and mostly in the copy phase (89% of mass), concentrated at recall_idx 1-3, i.e. the first few copy steps right after <DEL>. The largest activations (0.9-1.0 of max) come when the first copied token fed back in is s, at step L+1 in long sequences (L 8-9). Input s explains about 42% of mass. Weaker enrichment for inputs j/r/v/3 and outputs u/f/0/d/b. Almost silent in the original phase (except small activations at t=1-2) and never fires at t=0. No coherent predicate found: the best one (early copy & input s) scores F1 about 0.25 on dev, and broader token-set disjunctions reach 0.69 mass recall only at about 8% precision.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: s; t=2: s, z; t=5: s, v, l, z) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: u, f, 0, b; delimiter step: s, 3, x, g; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, t=2, t=1.
